name: חיבור וחיסור שלושה שברים עם מכנים מספריים (באנגלית)

functions.name: igcd2
functions.body: if q=0 then abs(p) else igcd2(q,mod(p,q))

questiontext:
Express the following as a single fraction in its lowest terms:

\[ \frac{{CT:0}}{{CT:1}}+\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:3}}-\frac{{CT:4}}{{CT:5}}. \]

[[input:ans]]
[[validation:ans]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Bring all three fractions to one common denominator, combine the numerators, then cancel any common factor.
Step 1 — A common denominator for all three fractions
When dealing with more than one fraction you can either focus on just two fractions at a time or, alternatively, you can find a suitable common factor for all the fractions and then perform all the arithmetic in one step. Using the latter technique in this example, with the product of the denominators \({{CT:1}}\cdot {{CT:3}}\cdot {{CT:5}}={{CT:6}}\):

\[ \frac{{CT:0}}{{CT:1}}+\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:3}}-\frac{{CT:4}}{{CT:5}} = \frac{{CT:7}}{{CT:6}}+\frac{{CT:8}}{{CT:6}}-\frac{{CT:9}}{{CT:6}} \]

Step 2 — Open the brackets and collect like terms
Write everything over the common denominator; careful with the minus sign in front of the third fraction, it changes the sign of every term of its numerator:

\[ \frac{{{CT:10}}+\left({{CT:11}}\right)-\left({{CT:12}}\right)}{{{CT:6}}}=\frac{{{CT:13}}}{{{CT:6}}} \]

Step 3 — Lowest terms
[[if test="{{CT:18}}"]]The numerator and the denominator have the common factor \({{CT:14}}\); cancel it:

\[ \frac{{{CT:13}}}{{{CT:6}}}=\frac{{{CT:14}}\left({{CT:15}}\right)}{{{CT:14}}\cdot {{CT:16}}} \]

Now nothing else cancels, so the fraction is in its lowest terms:[[else]]The numerator and the denominator have no common factor other than \(1\), so the fraction is already in its lowest terms:[[/if]]

\[ \frac{{CT:0}}{{CT:1}}+\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:3}}-\frac{{CT:4}}{{CT:5}} = \frac{{CT:7}}{{CT:6}}+\frac{{CT:8}}{{CT:6}}-\frac{{CT:9}}{{CT:6}} = {{CT:17}}. \]

on_true.feedback: Your answer is not in its simplest form but is otherwise correct.
